title: Perform seed testing processes and procedures to determine the physical and physiological quality of seed

lessons.title: Physical quality tests: purity, other seeds and moisture
lessons.html:
From submitted sample to working sample

On receipt, register the sample, check seals and labels against the request, and record its condition. Obtain working samples using an approved divider; the working sample mass for each test is specified per species in the ISTA rules. Retain the remainder for possible retesting.

Purity analysis

  1. Weigh the working sample to the precision required by the rules.
  2. Separate it into three components on a purity board, with forceps, magnification, sieves and a blower where appropriate:
    • Pure seed: seeds of the species stated, including those meeting the pure seed definitions for that species, even if immature, undersized or damaged within defined limits.
    • Other seeds: seeds of any other plant species.
    • Inert matter: seed fragments beyond the defined limits, soil, stones, chaff, stems and other non-seed material.
  3. Weigh each component; check that the sum is close to the original mass within the allowed limit, otherwise repeat.
  4. Calculate percentages by mass, rounded as the rules require.

The Pure Seed Definitions in the rules decide borderline cases; learn and apply them for each species tested.

Determination of other seeds by number

Examine a larger sample for seeds of specified other species, such as prohibited weeds, and report them by number. This test is important because a lot can have high purity but still carry seeds of noxious weeds.

Moisture content

The reference method is oven drying under specified temperature and time for each species, often after grinding for large seeds. Work quickly so the sample does not gain or lose moisture, use duplicate determinations and check that they agree within tolerance. Rapid electronic meters are useful for routine checks but must be calibrated against the oven method.

Thousand-seed weight

Count replicates of pure seed, weigh them and calculate the mass of 1 000 seeds. Check that replicate variation is within the limit.

Laboratory safety

Treated seed requires gloves and dust control; grinders and ovens need guarding and heat protection; blowers should be used with extraction.

lessons.title: Physiological quality tests: germination, viability and vigour
lessons.html:
Germination test

  1. Take pure seeds from the purity analysis; count replicates as the rules require, usually 400 seeds in replicates.
  2. Plant on the prescribed substrate: paper (top of paper, between paper, pleated), sand or organic growing media.
  3. Apply the prescribed temperature regime, light conditions and moisture; use dormancy-breaking treatments when specified, such as prechilling or potassium nitrate.
  4. Make first and final counts on the days specified for the species.
  5. Evaluate each seedling as normal or abnormal using the seedling evaluation criteria; classify remaining seeds as hard, fresh or dead.
  6. Check that replicates agree within the tolerance; retest if they do not.
  7. Report the percentage of normal seedlings, abnormal seedlings, hard, fresh and dead seeds.

Germinator and substrate control

  • Monitor and record germinator temperatures continuously; investigate excursions.
  • Check substrate quality: paper and sand must be free of toxic substances and of suitable pH and water holding.
  • Prevent contamination between tests; clean germinators and trays regularly.

Tetrazolium (TZ) viability test

Seeds are imbibed, prepared (cut or pierced), and soaked in tetrazolium salt solution. Living tissue stains red; dead tissue remains unstained. The analyst evaluates staining patterns of essential structures to classify each seed as viable or non-viable. TZ gives quick results and detects viability in dormant seed, but interpretation requires training.

Vigour tests

TestPrincipleCommon use
Accelerated ageingHigh temperature and humidity stress before germinationSoybeans and many others
Electrical conductivityLeakage of electrolytes from damaged membranesPeas, soybeans
Cold testGermination after cold, wet soil exposureMaize

Follow the validated method exactly; small changes in temperature or time change results.

Reporting results

Report using the format required, with sample identification, methods used and any deviations. Check calculations and have results reviewed before release.

Key points

  • Obtain working samples with approved dividers and retain the remainder.
  • Purity separates pure seed, other seeds and inert matter using the Pure Seed Definitions.
  • Moisture reference method is oven drying under specified conditions.
  • Germination counts only normal seedlings and requires replicate tolerance checks.
  • TZ shows viability; vigour tests predict field performance.
